label: no
controls_available: Simplified console latch buttons: Slide left, Slide right, TALLER, WIDER, and COAST.
Each console click sets a persistent control until another console click; CERTIFY is administrative.
The full-mode body-arrow hold surface is hidden in simplified mode.
autonomous_processes: Each 40 ms task tick runs four physics substeps: morphing changes height, horizontal input updates capped velocity with drag, gravity updates vertical velocity, collision checks land or stop motion, and seal contact is collected.
Between console clicks the current latch remains active; after COAST, residual horizontal velocity decays while gravity, landing, and seal checks continue.
The render loop advances the simulation to elapsed task time and redraws the parcel, platforms, seals, and collected-seal count.
grouped_control_modes: D_console_latch: all active simplified-mode outcome-affecting console clicks (left, right, taller, wider, and COAST) across all seeds and occurrences; CERTIFY and NEW ROOM are administrative.

clause_i.reason: At difficulty 2 the supplied parameters omit the island layout, so generation uses one left-to-right linear room with only bounded positional offsets. The source task records a known simplified blind route, and the replay dynamics support a fixed phase schedule chosen only from the agent's own action times (WIDER, RIGHT, TALLER, braking LEFT/RIGHT, WIDER, RIGHT, TALLER, LEFT, then COAST). Thus q can select the route-stage latch from I_t without the visible window; the several mid-run latches make this an observation-free interactive route, not a pre-run solution. No choice of D, Delta, or w makes visual evidence necessary for this exact grouped mode.

clause_ii.reason: The canvas visibly renders the solids, gold-seal locations, parcel position, parcel height/width, and collected count. Three chronological frames over the configured 80 ms window can additionally reveal recent parcel motion, so a bounded-window policy g can choose an action from the visible room and trajectory (or simply ignore the window and follow q). This clause alone does not repair the failed conjunction.

clause_iii.reason: The same active parcel physics creates a local degrading opportunity at the unsupported gap. For example, when a narrow, right-moving parcel is still salvageable near the gap, delivering WIDER immediately can widen it and preserve support; waiting while the current control and gravity advance moves it farther into the gap, leaving success possible for an interior delayed state but reducing WIDER's success value/advantage. The loss is caused by visible non-clock motion and falling, not by a deadline or later completion.

common_visible_process: The candidate common process for clauses (ii) and (iii) is the rendered parcel's inertial slide, shape morphing, gravity, and support loss while it traverses the overhead shelf and the 85-unit gap. It is visibly observable and can make a delayed intervention valuable, but clause (i) fails because this L2 simplified route admits an observation-free time-scheduled latch policy.

pre_run.reason: There is no separate startable autonomous outcome phase in this implementation: the parcel is active as soon as it is rendered, and each latch remains an outcome-affecting control. A successful linear-room route must change shape during the run: the overhead shelf requires a short/wide parcel (clearance 58), the upper seal is at reach 160 and requires a tall parcel, the gap requires the parcel to become wide enough to bridge or otherwise cross safely, and the final seal again requires greater height. Therefore no generated instance admits a solution that, after preparation, sends no more outcome-affecting actions until the outcome phase ends. The documented blind route uses multiple mid-run latches and does not meet the frozen pre-run criterion.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 2 is the easy profile with clearance 58, gap 85, reach 160, alcove 0, and drag 0.85; it contains no island layout parameter.
Both full and simplified interactions are implemented, and the exact runtime settings are an 80 ms observation window with three frames.

The generator uses the supplied difficulty parameters; without layout=island it builds the linear room, randomizing only bounded tunnel, shelf length, gap-start, and seal positions while preserving the same route structure.

The linear world has area 6400, height bounds 32-200, 40 ms ticks, 4500 max ticks, and an active initial parcel at x=100, bottom=420, height=80; the control condition is exported to public state and truth.
The browser physics changes height, velocity, position, gravity, support/landing, seal collection, and terminal status autonomously on every tick.
Simplified mode is selected from the condition; the canvas visibly draws solids, seals, and parcel geometry, and tick advances to elapsed performance.now time before redrawing.
Simplified console clicks call set with the selected latch control, while the animation frame loop continues to tick the active simulation.
The visible body-control and console surfaces use the hidden attribute, so the simplified render can expose only the console controls.
The runner configuration confirms play_time_seconds 180, observation_window_ms 80, frames_per_observation 3, and an 80 ms step cycle.
The browser exposes a virtual task clock through elapsed time and performance.now, distinct from native wall time.
The shared clock can run a bounded task-time observation window and pause at its exact task-time endpoint, so the 80 ms setting is task progress rather than provider latency.
The grader independently replays the same four-substep morphing, inertial, gravity, collision, and seal-collection dynamics and marks falling/timeout/solved outcomes.
Grading binds the transcript to the exact condition and simplified console_latch input source, replays every event at its task tick, and requires the replayed state to be solved.
The verifier loads the exported result and delegates outcome verification to the independent Concertina Courier grader.
The reference controller uses short prediction/coast commands, showing that physical control is about current motion; this solver's private state access is not treated as policy information.
The linear branch follows a reusable sequence of shape and movement phases, while the island branch is the one that needs a different layout; the solver is implementation evidence only.

The visible task describes morphing, unsupported falling, and simplified click/COAST controls, and its source note explicitly identifies the L2 linear configuration as having a simplified blind route.
The shared verifier helper loads the mechanic grader and reads the exported task result; it does not replace the physical replay.

uncertainties: task.json retains default L3/full capability metadata, so the supplied case condition and controls.json L2/simplified profile were used for this classification.
The reference solver reads private browser state for wiring tests; that implementation detail was not treated as information available to a screenshot-only policy.
